channel.title: The Wang Report · Science and Health
channel.description: The Wang Report Science and Health desk: daily briefings and weekly columns.

item.title: An Interstellar Comet's Ice Carries Ten Times The Solar System's Heavy Hydrogen
item.description: Comet 3I/ATLAS, photographed from Mars, holds ice far richer in deuterium than the solar system's, and the number works as a thermometer for a place we cannot visit.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: Two New Species Found in a Motel Room Project Bear on How Complex Life Began
item.description: A scrappy project has turned up two new species of a rare organism, and the one thing the report says about them is that they could shed light on how simple cells became complex ones.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: Commonwealth Fusion Systems Buys 6,200 Miles Of Magnet Tape, And The Tape Is The Point
item.description: The fusion company's record order is for the superconducting ribbon that its reactor magnets are wound from, which is where the economics of a compact machine get decided.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: A Dozen Years of New Chemotherapy Drugs Added an Average of 2.1 Months of Life
item.description: Pooled across every new chemotherapy drug approved over that span, the average overall survival benefit is 2.1 months, a number worth holding against the longevity industry's pricing.
item.dc:creator: Sora Whitlam

item.title: Starship Reaches Orbit On Flight 14 And Deploys Starlink Satellites
item.description: After more than three years of test flights from Texas, the rocket has reached orbit and put payload into it, which turns a test article into something with a customer.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: Anthropic's 950-Agent Swarm Finds A New Enzyme In 21 Hours
item.description: Anthropic's new life-sciences lab ran 950 AI agents against public DNA for 21 hours and flagged a genuinely new enzyme system, but no regulator yet knows how to audit a machine's own judgment about what counts as a discovery.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: 8.8 Million Adults Later, HHS's Ultra-Processed Definition Is Still in Review
item.description: The largest ultra-processed food study ever assembled found dose-dependent harm in 8.8 million adults, landing exactly as HHS decides whether the evidence is finally strong enough to regulate.
item.dc:creator: Sora Whitlam

item.title: The CAR-T That Ignores CD19 On Purpose
item.description: PeproMene Bio's BAFF-R CAR-T put seven of nine relapsed lymphoma patients into remission, showing that switching the target antigen, not re-dosing it, may be what rescues CAR-T failures.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: A Second CAR-T Target Rescues Relapsed Patients
item.description: A Phase 1 trial rescued lymphoma patients whose CD19 CAR-T had already failed with a second target, BAFF-R, though nine patients isn't proof it scales.
item.dc:creator: Sora Whitlam

item.title: A Single Gene Edit Holds At One Year
item.description: CRISPR Therapeutics' one-time liver edit kept cholesterol and triglycerides down a year after infusion, proving durability for the first time, though the company's own protocol tracks these patients for years past this readout.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: Moderna's $45 Billion Bet On A Sealed Number
item.description: Wall Street revalued Moderna by $45 billion on a topline label alone, and the number that would actually justify that move stays sealed until October.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: A Demo Video Doing A Prospectus's Job
item.description: Deep Robotics timed a single-take video of a robot climbing stairs to the week China's humanoid IPO mania peaked, because four units sold in two years can't do that job.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: Fugaku Lost To A Seven-Hour Quantum Run
item.description: IBM's open Quantum Advantage Tracker matters less as proof quantum computers won and more as published circuits that more than 30 outside teams have now tried, and failed, to break.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: A Stablecoin Issuer Becomes A Neurotech Funder
item.description: Tether, the company behind the world's largest stablecoin, has quietly become a serious funder of brain implants for paralysis, and its reserve-driven balance sheet may outlast biotech's usual venture cycle.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: The Rocket Problem Just Became A Starship Factory Problem
item.description: Starship's 13th flight proved the ship survives and the payload works in the same mission, which means the real bottleneck now sits in the satellite factory, not the rocket.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: China's Brain Chip Market Outruns Its Patients
item.description: Neuracle's brain implant has treated 32 patients and earned zero revenue, yet Beijing built a reimbursement code, and Neuracle filed a $345m IPO, faster than the clinical evidence justifies.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: Brain Implants Are Not All Equally Hard
item.description: This week paired a bidirectional touch-restoring brain implant with China's first commercial brain-computer interface, and the commercial one, despite the bigger headline, is solving the easier engineering problem.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield
